Smt Vaseela And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12
February, 2024

Author: Vivek Varma
Bench: Vivek Varma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:24637
Court No. - 87
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 6407 of 2022
Applicant :- Smt Vaseela And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Narendra Singh Chahar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Awadh Sharma
Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and Sri Awadh Sharma,
counsel for the opposite party no.2.
2.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the entire proceedings of Case No. 77 of 2022 (State vs. Vaseela and another), pending before the court of Civil Judge (S.D.), F.T.C.,
Ghaziabad, under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 504 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act and 3/4 Muslim Marriage Act, P.S. Loni Border, District Ghaziabad as well as to quash the charge-sheet dated 16.8.2021 arising out of case Crime No. 523 of 2021, including the cognizance order dated 6.1.2022 passed by Civil Judge (S.D.), F.T.C., Ghaziabad, on the basis of compromise between the parties.

sentences.text:
In compliance to the order passed by this Court dated 16.3.2022 the Civil Judge (Sr. Division)/
F.T.C., Ghaziabad has sent his report dated 15.6.2022, according to which the compromise deed had been filed by the parties before the Court and the same has been verified vide order dated 30.5.2022.

A copy of the compromise deed and the order of the trial court dated 30.5.2022 are annexed with the report of the Civil Judge (Sr. Division)/ F.T.C., Ghaziabad.
6.

It is submitted by the counsel for the applicants that if the criminal prosecution is allowed to proceed it may create further complication in the otherwise normal relationship that is arising between the hitherto bitterly estranged couple and their families.
7. Sri Awadh Sharma, counsel for the opposite party no. 2 submits that the opposite party no.2 has no objection if the proceedings of the aforesaid case are quashed.
He does not dispute the submissions advanced by the counsel for the applicants or the correctness of the documents relied upon by him.

8. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing such a prosecution to proceed any further.

9. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T., 2008 (9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.
